cls: Somatostatin analogue / inhibitory peptide hormone (antihemorrhagic / antisecretory)
pharm: A 14-amino-acid cyclic peptide hormone that inhibits secretion of growth hormone, glucagon, insulin, and gastroenteropancreatic hormones, and reduces splanchnic blood flow and portal pressure
quick: IV bolus 250 mcg over ~3 min, then continuous infusion 250 mcg/h; continue 48-120 h
Avoid unless essential; safety in pregnancy not established
No specific dose adjustment established; use with caution
Used in variceal bleeding from portal hypertension; no specific dose reduction
Blood glucose, blood pressure/heart rate, bleeding control, infusion continuity
summary: Somatostatin is a naturally occurring 14-amino-acid inhibitory peptide hormone administered as a continuous intravenous infusion. By suppressing secretion of multiple gastrointestinal and pancreatic hormones and reducing splanchnic blood flow and portal pressure, it is used (in Europe and other regions) to control acute bleeding from esophageal/gastric varices and other severe upper GI bleeding, and to treat pancreatic and intestinal fistulas. It has a very short half-life, so an initial bolus is followed by continuous infusion. Somatostatin is not FDA-approved; the longer-acting analogue octreotide is used in the US.
indications: Acute severe bleeding from esophageal or gastric varices (adjunct, in portal hypertension)
Acute severe bleeding from gastric or duodenal ulcers / erosive or hemorrhagic gastritis
Treatment of pancreatic, biliary, and intestinal fistulas (as an adjunct)
Prevention of complications following pancreatic surgery

dosage.d: Initial slow IV bolus of 250 mcg over about 3 minutes, then continuous IV infusion of 250 mcg/hour
dosage.t: Continue infusion for 48 to 120 hours (commonly until 48-72 h after bleeding stops)
dosage.n: A further bolus may be given if the infusion is interrupted for more than 3-5 minutes

dosage.d: Continuous IV infusion of 250 mcg/hour (3.5 mcg/kg/hour)
dosage.t: Continued until the fistula closes, then tapered before stopping
dosage.n: Withdraw gradually over 1-3 days to avoid rebound

admin: Reconstitute the lyophilized powder with the supplied/physiological saline diluent immediately before use
Give the initial bolus as a slow IV injection over about 3 minutes
Administer the maintenance dose as an uninterrupted continuous IV infusion via pump
If the infusion is interrupted for more than 3-5 minutes, restart with a new bolus (very short half-life)
Monitor blood glucose during therapy; do not mix with glucose-containing solutions unless specified
moa: Somatostatin is the natural inhibitory peptide hormone. It inhibits the release of growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone, and gastroenteropancreatic hormones including glucagon, insulin, gastrin, secretin, and vasoactive intestinal peptide. It reduces splanchnic (mesenteric) blood flow and portal venous pressure without major systemic arterial effects, and decreases gastric acid and pancreatic exocrine secretion - effects that underlie its use in variceal/GI bleeding and fistulas.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to somatostatin or any excipient
relative: Insulin-dependent diabetes (alters glucose homeostasis - close monitoring needed)

preg: Safety in human pregnancy has not been established. Somatostatin should be avoided during pregnancy unless considered essential by the treating clinician and the expected benefit outweighs the potential risk.
lact: It is not known whether somatostatin is excreted in human milk. Breastfeeding should be avoided during treatment because of a lack of safety data.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is established for renal impairment; use with caution and monitor.
hepatic: Somatostatin is used in patients with portal hypertension and hepatic disease for variceal bleeding; no specific dose reduction is recommended, but monitor closely.

moderate: Insulin and oral hypoglycemic agents - somatostatin alters glucose homeostasis (initial transient hypoglycemia, then hyperglycemia by inhibiting insulin); adjust antidiabetic therapy and monitor glucose
Drugs metabolized after intestinal absorption (e.g. cimetidine) - absorption may be altered by reduced GI motility/secretion
minor: Agents potentiating bradycardia - monitor heart rate
interactions.diagnostics: Suppresses multiple GI/pancreatic hormone levels, which can confound endocrine testing during the infusion

common: Transient changes in blood glucose (early hypoglycemia, later hyperglycemia)
serious: Bradycardia and changes in blood pressure (especially with rapid bolus)
Rebound hormone hypersecretion on abrupt withdrawal

monitoring: Blood glucose at regular intervals (e.g. every 3-4 hours initially)
Continuity of the infusion (avoid interruptions >3-5 minutes)
counsel: This medicine is given as a continuous drip in hospital to control bleeding or reduce fluid losses
Your blood sugar, heart rate, and blood pressure will be checked regularly
Tell the team if you feel sweaty, shaky, dizzy, flushed, or unwell
The infusion should not be stopped suddenly without medical supervision
pk: Rapid onset of hormonal/hemodynamic effects after IV bolus
Effects established quickly during continuous infusion
Very short - approximately 1 to 3 minutes in the circulation
Effects cease rapidly after stopping the infusion; rebound hypersecretion may occur on abrupt withdrawal
Store the lyophilized powder per the product label (typically refrigerated 2-8 C or below 25 C); use reconstituted solution immediately
pearls: Not FDA-approved - native somatostatin is used in Europe and other regions; in the US the longer-acting analogue octreotide is used instead. This record is based on EMA/SmPC and BNF data.
Extremely short half-life (~1-3 min) mandates an initial bolus followed by an uninterrupted continuous infusion - re-bolus if the line stops for more than a few minutes
Reduces splanchnic blood flow and portal pressure - useful adjunct in acute variceal and other upper GI bleeding alongside endoscopic therapy
Causes biphasic blood-glucose changes (transient early hypoglycemia, then hyperglycemia from insulin suppression) - monitor glucose closely, especially in diabetics
Taper rather than stop abruptly to avoid rebound hormone hypersecretion
missed: Not applicable - somatostatin is given as a clinician-controlled continuous IV infusion in hospital, not as discrete self-administered doses. If the infusion is interrupted for more than 3-5 minutes, a new loading bolus is given because of the very short half-life.
overdose: There is limited experience with somatostatin overdose. Excessive dosing or rapid administration may produce pronounced disturbances of glucose homeostasis (hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia), bradycardia, and blood pressure changes. Management is to stop or reduce the infusion and provide supportive care with blood glucose monitoring and correction; given the very short half-life, effects resolve quickly after discontinuation.
